hypotheses.claim: slice tab=0 scores 0.3044 vs overall 0.6191 across 5579 users; a feature or prior targeted at this slice should close part of the gap

evidence.finding: 56% of the gain survives surface scrambling: mechanism revised from surface familiarity to partitioned familiarity (about half surface-specific, half counting structure). Promotion unaffected (validation-based).

control.detail: R33-placebo valid 0.61612 vs control 0.61715: the entire +0.0024 gain collapses when the per-surface count is detached from its impression

hypotheses.claim: slice tab=1 scores 0.5949 vs overall 0.6191 across 20119 users; a feature or prior targeted at this slice should close part of the gap; oracle headroom on the overall metric 0.2128 (31% of the slice's users are all-negative inside it, so the slice-restricted score understates the model)

evidence.note: Claimable negative: -0.00347 clears the 0.002 gate, consistent across 3 seeds and both metric components (valid GAUC 0.68969 vs 0.69341, nDCG@5 0.54444 vs 0.54568). Session-local outcome momentum is a coarser, reset-on-gap duplicate of hist10/hist30.

evidence.finding: The within-visit fatigue effect is real and large marginally (tab=1 long_view rate 0.418 at session position 0 -> 0.143 at 50+, train rows) and 77% of its prior variance is WITHIN user, the only channel the metric scores; 54% of that within-user prior is not explained by the champion's features (R^2 0.46). For tab_n -- the feature that DID win, +0.0024 -- the same measurement gives 86% novel and 1.04e-04 of within-user prior variance, versus sess_pos's 8.19e-05: the same order. So a 'large, novel, within-user prior' screen would have rated sess_pos as promising as tab_n and been wrong. That screen is hereby falsified as a pre-run filter for this project.
evidence.scope: What is refuted is this INTERVENTION, not the slice's headroom: tab=1 is 73% of impressions and its oracle headroom (0.2113) is an arithmetic fact about slice size, not a defect the loop has explained away.

hypotheses.claim: slice hist=31-100 scores 0.6215 vs overall 0.6206 across 10947 users; a feature or prior targeted at this slice should close part of the gap; oracle headroom on the overall metric 0.1322 (28% of the slice's users are all-negative inside it, so the slice-restricted score understates the model)

evidence.note: The tag partition denominator, the arm the hypothesis was really about. Below control on validation and on both metric components (valid GAUC 0.69185 vs 0.69341, nDCG@5 0.54459 vs 0.54568) and on the hist=31-100 diagnostic slice itself (0.62056 vs 0.62227), so the loss is not a trade of the slice against everything else. Under the 0.002 claim bar, so recorded as directional, not as a claimed negative.

evidence.finding: Second and stronger falsification of the additive-prior screen. On the identical instrument iteration 1 used, tag_n carries 4.871e-04 of NOVEL within-user prior variance (85% novel after regression on the champion) against the winning tab_n's 3.656e-04: the loser has 1.33x the winner's novel signal, and it varies within 73.2% of valid users against tab_n's 43.7%. Iteration 1's loser scored 0.79x on the same axis. The screen now fails in both directions -- it rated one loser equal to the winner and rates this one ABOVE the winner -- so it is not merely imprecise, it is uninformative. Redundancy is separately ruled out and in the surprising direction: conditioning tag_n on the shipped tag_hist INCREASES its rate variance 12x (0.00057 -> 0.00685), i.e. tag_hist masks the exposure effect marginally rather than absorbing it.
evidence.scope: What is refuted is this INTERVENTION and the generalisation behind it (that tab_n won because it was a partitioned exposure count, so the same construction on the tag and author partitions should also win). The slice's headroom (0.13222) remains an arithmetic fact about slice size; the slice scores ABOVE the model average and was never a defect.
evidence.candidate_discriminator_untested: The two constructions differ in one structural way: the partition KEY is a field the model can condition on for tab (BASE carries tab) and for author (author_id), but tag identity is not in the feature set at all -- tag_hist is an outcome count, not the tag. A per-partition count is a conditional quantity, and tag_n may be unbindable to what it counts. Weak directional support: auth_n, whose key IS a field, recovered +0.00024 on top of tag_n despite being constant within 75% of valid users. Far under noise. Untested, and offered as the next candidate, not as a finding.

hypotheses.claim: slice dur=4 scores 0.5404 vs overall 0.6206 across 8023 users; a feature or prior targeted at this slice should close part of the gap; oracle headroom on the overall metric 0.0439, of which 0.0022 is EXCESS over a matched null slice (same users, same per-user row counts, rows drawn at random) and therefore attributable to the model rather than to slice size; 56% of the slice's users are all-negative inside it, so the slice-restricted score understates the model
